# Twining -- Mandatory Tool Usage Gates

You have Twining MCP tools for persistent project coordination. You MUST follow these three gates for EVERY task.

## Gate 1: Context Assembly (BEFORE any work)
You MUST call `twining_assemble` with your task description and narrowest relevant scope BEFORE reading code or making changes. You MUST call `twining_why` on files you plan to modify. NEVER start working without these calls -- skipping them creates blind decisions that conflict with existing work.

## Gate 2: Decision Recording (AFTER choices)
You MUST call `twining_decide` for any architectural or implementation choice where alternatives exist. Always include specific rationale and at least one rejected alternative. Post `finding` entries for surprising discoveries, `warning` entries for gotchas, and `need` entries for follow-up work via `twining_post`. NEVER use `twining_post` with entry_type `decision` -- always use `twining_decide`.

## Gate 3: Verification (BEFORE completing)
You MUST call `twining_verify` on your working scope before telling the user the task is done. Post a `status` entry summarizing what you accomplished. Link commits to decisions via `twining_link_commit` after committing.

## Critical Rules
- Scopes use path prefixes: use `src/auth/` not `project` -- always use the narrowest scope that covers the affected area.
- NEVER skip Gate 1 (assembly) -- this is the #1 cause of wasted work and conflicting decisions.
- NEVER skip Gate 3 (verification) -- unverified work leaves gaps for the next agent.
- NEVER record decisions via `twining_post` -- always use `twining_decide` which provides conflict detection and rationale tracking.

## Anti-patterns to Avoid
- Blind decisions: Making choices without calling `twining_assemble` first. You WILL miss existing decisions and create conflicts.
- Scope inflation: Using `project` scope when the work only affects a specific module. Narrow scopes keep assembly relevant.
- Fire-and-forget: Recording a decision but never linking it to commits or running verification. Always follow through to Gate 3.
